checks.finding: Runner RL, reward, and CE equations match the upstream notebook algebra.
Runner uses G=2 while upstream uses G=4; sigma=0.4 and masked zero-mean projection otherwise match.
Marker masks are boolean, valid markers are true, perturbations and losses mask invalid options, and attention padding is zero.
Both paths autocast only the model forward to FP16 and cast logits to FP32 before loss construction.
Runner aborts immediately after unscale on any non-finite gradient; upstream passes directly to scaler.step(), which is designed to skip an overflowed step and reduce the scale.
The executed artifact contains neither loss values nor offending parameter names. Current diagnostic code was added after the recorded run, and no executed-script hash was retained.

Runtime accounting is internally consistent: 421293827 named parameters plus a three-element temperature buffer equals 421293830 state elements. The runner intentionally excludes the 263938-parameter action head, unlike upstream.
One forward and backward reached 3873439744 peak reserved bytes, below 11.5 GiB; Adam state allocation and a completed step were not measured.

Default GradScaler initial scaling overflow is the leading explanation. FP16 attention/backward instability remains possible; the artifact cannot distinguish these causes. The RL and CE values were not retained.

safest_next_diagnostic.specification: Run exactly one otherwise-identical forward and backward with torch.amp.GradScaler('cuda', init_scale=1.0, growth_interval=2000), then unscale and stop without calling scaler.step, optimizer.step, or scaler.update. Persist combined, CE, and RL losses; reward extrema; scaler scale; finite/non-finite counts and first names separately for encoder and decision head; and peak memory.
safest_next_diagnostic.decision_rule: Finite unscaled gradients disproves intrinsic FP16-gradient failure and identifies default loss scaling as the prior blocker. Non-finite gradients at scale 1.0 confirms a model/autocast backward issue and justifies a separately authorized BF16 diagnostic.
